Centennial Jing-Zhang AI Innovation Belt / open co-creation submission

Herringbone Switchback: Urban Design for the Centennial Jing-Zhang AI Innovation Belt

Taking the Qinglongqiao herringbone switchback as a structural prototype, the 9.7 km by 1.37 km corridor is organised as two lines - a west heritage green spine and an east scenario belt - each standing on its own, engaging and exchanging dominance at a single apex in the AI Origin Community. This offline exhibition covers the overview map, three-level scopes, key areas, land-use partition, mobility, blue-green and public space, buildings and renewal projects, AI scenarios, core metrics, task coverage, self-check status, sources and assumptions. The authoritative data remain the GeoJSON layers and metrics.json.

Three-level scopes

The three levels are three different kinds of work, not three zoom levels of one drawing

design_brief.json

Coordinated research area, about 43.6 sq km

Answers what role the belt plays in the regional innovation network, yielding relational judgements and coordination mechanisms rather than a land-use plan. North produces technology and rules, the middle people and ecosystem, the south markets and revenue; the wings inject factors and scenarios.

Overall design area, about 11.4 sq km

Answers how the corridor itself holds together, yielding regulatory-depth urban design structure: land-use partition, slow mobility and roads, the blue-green and public-space skeleton, and renewal phasing - all expressed as recomputable layers.

Key detailed design area, about 368.4 ha

Answers how the three places that must move first become concrete, yielding frontage relationships, public-space components and scenario placement, approaching the depth of a comprehensive implementation plan. Recomputed total 369.3 ha, cross-checked against the announcement.

Key areas

Each key area takes one role in the reversal: descending leg, apex, climbing leg

key_areas.geojson

Dazhongsi AI Industry Cluster / descending leg

72.0 ha

The divider migrates east to about 26% of the corridor width; the spine widens and service land narrows into a compact continuous active frontage. AI-native consumption, business services and low-speed autonomous delivery are suggested to lead, converting northern innovation into market outcomes; frontage follows a small-grain, high-frequency principle.

Beijing AI Origin Community / the apex

104.3 ha

Where the two lines come closest to equal width, the spine widens into the herringbone apex plaza; plaza land bridges both lines and the east line yields dominance. Research alongside, living around, public at the centre; the plaza carries public AI experience, developer events and honour displays.

Zhongzhiyuan AI Acceleration Area / climbing leg

192.9 ha

The divider migrates west to about 62%, research land reaches its greatest width, and the spine narrows but stays continuous. Full-stack indigenous R&D is suggested to lead, alongside originating standards, evaluation and governance rules; research land sits hard against the spine, treating publicly accessible research frontage as a design objective.

Evidence of topological closure

Six land-use classes tile the design area completely. The divider is defined once, both sides reuse the same vertices, and everything is snapped to a 1 cm grid, so no gaps or overlaps exist.

Blue-green and public space: continuity over width

The spine is compressed by research land in the north but never broken: a continuous 9.7 km linear green space in central Beijing is irreplaceable while local width is expendable. Public space comprises the apex plaza and five transverse public corridors, letting publicness permeate sideways into the blocks. Protective green at the nodes also carries stormwater retention; blue-line positions and engineering methods must be confirmed by professional teams against official data.

Buildings: what is recomputed and what is not concluded

Illustrative buildings are nine clusters only: 22.68 ha of footprint, 1.99% of the design area, all on the east line, never on the spine or plaza, and inset from parcel edges to show setback relationships. Total floor area, floor area ratio and building height are statutory judgements with no official controls supplied, and are registered as status: unknown.

Why the middle goes first

The same as the construction order at Qinglongqiao: the reversal point is the link the structure cannot do without, and both legs depend on it. Once the apex plaza and the two adjacent stitch corridors are built, the corridor immediately has a usable public core and crossable transverse links; beginning from the ends would leave both lines dead-ended until the middle was complete. Renewal starts from public space and frontage; demolition is never the means of starting. Phasing is a concept suggestion for discussion, not a development sequence or an approval arrangement.

AI scenarios

Ten scenario cards plus three industry test scenarios, each stating its users, location, data boundary and human-review step

agent.2 · 10 scenario cards
01 Spine walkability diagnosis

Public footfall and break data assist in identifying pedestrian discontinuities; the improvement list is professionally reviewed before it enters design.

02 Shared right of way for low-speed delivery

Time-shared use of the east belt and stitch streets by low-speed delivery and slow mobility; extent and hours require professional assessment.

03 Crossing-safety support at stitch nodes

Assists in identifying conflict patterns at the five nodes, producing design suggestions only, with no conclusions on signal control.

04 Event-day crowd modelling on the plaza

Distribution and egress suggestions for large events; the actual plan is decided by people.

05 Testbed booking and conflict coordination

Coordinates time and space conflicts at northern facilities so testing does not obstruct public passage.

06 Enterprise service copilot

Navigation of policy, space, compliance and event information for AI firms and small teams, limited to public material.

07 Accessibility route verification

Verifies wheelchair and low-vision routes from public maps and field feedback, producing retrofit suggestions.

08 Heritage narrative guidance

Historical interpretation along the spine, limited to already public historical material and never distorting the record.

09 Night-time inspection support

Environmental sensing helps identify lighting and sightline blind spots; no facial recognition, no individual tracking.

10 Maintenance ticket generation

Identifies damaged paving, planting and fittings and raises tickets; disposal remains with the managing body.

Three industry test-and-verification scenarios

The northern open testbed (a bookable outdoor test area), the low-speed vehicle corridor along the east line (a continuous test route time-shared with slow mobility), and public-interaction verification on the apex plaza (replaceable positions for interaction devices). Together they form a progression from closed to semi-open to public verification, along which a product can climb stage by stage - logically the same move as the switchback itself.

Privacy and human-review boundary

Collect no unnecessary personal data, perform no facial recognition or individual tracking, use no non-public data, subject every output affecting the public to human review before execution, and always provide a non-participating alternative. A test scenario is not approved operation; anything touching public safety or ethical compliance requires authorisation from the competent authority.
